check: adversarial audit of AKHANDA's own claims
standard: a claim SURVIVES only when a genuine attempt to falsify it ran and failed; anything that could not be attacked is UNFALSIFIABLE, which is an unmeasured claim rather than a strong one

claims.attack: count signature magic bytes present in the filler itself
claims.detail: The filler contains 1042 signature-header occurrences across 3 types in 64 MB, and the carver still reported no false positives — so it rejected them on structure, not by never seeing one.

claims.attack: assert each mutation actually changes the signed bytes
claims.detail: all 7 mutations genuinely move the signed preimage and all 7 are caught, including the tool_ref forgery that only became possible after ENTRY_VERSION 3

delete_middle.reason: seq out of order at index 2

reorder.reason: seq out of order at index 1

claims.attack: delete the JPEG signature and re-replay the pinned cases
claims.detail: baseline {'REPRODUCED': 5} -> with JPEG removed {'DRIFTED': 5} -> restored {'REPRODUCED': 5}. The gate fails when the carver changes and recovers when it is put back.

claims.attack: feed it clean, tampered and wrong-version chains
claims.detail: clean exits 0, tampered exits 1, an ENTRY_VERSION 2 chain exits 1. It discriminates rather than always passing.

claims.asserted: bad sectors are skipped, logged and signed
claims.attack: count the raises, then try to hide the skipped ranges from the digest
claims.detail: the fixture raised EIO 2 times in the real write path; the result records 1 range(s), refuses VERIFIED, accounts for every byte, and removing bad_ranges CHANGES the signed digest (True)

claims.attack: scan every test for a missing assertion or a tautological one
claims.detail: all 562 collected test functions carry a real assertion or an expected-raise

claims.asserted: deleting a whole device from a case is detected
claims.attack: confirm the surviving chains still verify, so the root does the work
claims.detail: every surviving chain verifies perfectly on its own, and only the case root notices the deletion — so the finding is not an artefact of the chains breaking

claims.asserted: tool_ref identifies the build that wrote an entry
claims.attack: change a real constant in a real attested module and re-derive the digest
claims.detail: changing BLOCK_SIZE in erasure/engine.py moved the digest c508412d47c60e56 -> fee0ee0831ffe9ff, and reverting restored it
